title: al-Laʿb al-Nabawi: A Warm Embrace and Play Before Guidance
summary: The Prophet ﷺ would play with his grandchildren, carry them, and laugh with them. At this stage, dramatic play is the child’s natural language—Vygotsky describes it as a primary tool for acquiring rules, self-regulation, and building perspective. When a parent integrates play with stories from the seerah, learning transforms from external commands into an internal experience. This lesson offers the parent two practical models for daily cognitive play: narrating a short story in your own voice while holding a puppet, and joining your child in retelling the story in their own way.
try_this: This week: Choose a short story from the seerah (such as the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, his hijrah, or the plot of the disbelievers in the valley). Narrate the story to your child while holding a puppet or toy, using your own voice. Let them interrupt and ask questions. If they retell the story in their own way, the lesson has succeeded—do not correct the details, just celebrate their storytelling.
reflection_prompts: Have you noticed your child remembering details from the story that you didn’t expect?
When was the last time you sat on the floor together to retell a story from childhood?
